summary.headline: Wipro Q1 FY27 IT services revenue rose 0.9% YoY in constant currency to $2.61B, with Q2 guided to -1.5% to +0.5% sequential.
summary.overview: Wipro's Q1 FY27 IT services revenue was $2.61B, up 0.9% YoY and down 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, within guidance. Operating margin fell 1.2 points YoY to 16%, which management attributed to salary increases, large-deal ramp-ups, AI investments and acquisition integration, partly offset by rupee depreciation. Order bookings were $3.4B, including $1.6B from 13 large deals. Q2 guidance is $2.574B to $2.627B, implying -1.5% to +0.5% sequential growth, and management declined to forecast beyond Q2.

financial_highlights.change: Large deal bookings $1.6B from 13 deals; Vibhor Singhal cited total bookings of $3.3B in Q&A
Over $3B returned to shareholders in last 12 months, including this dividend

segments.name: Americas 1
segments.commentary: Flattish YoY and down 2.3% QoQ in constant currency.

segments.name: Americas 2
segments.commentary: Declined 7.3% YoY and 2.5% QoQ in constant currency.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY but declined 0.9% QoQ; BFSI, technology and communication strong, energy, manufacturing and resources soft.

segments.name: APMEA
segments.commentary: Grew 13.5% YoY and 4.4% QoQ, the strongest region this quarter.

segments.name: BFSI sector
segments.commentary: Up 2.6% YoY but down 1.2% QoQ; management cited slipped discretionary decisions and ramp-up delays on large deals.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Down 2.6% QoQ and 3.0% YoY, driven by US payer and provider budget pressure.

segments.name: Energy, resources and manufacturing (EMR)
segments.commentary: Down 3.6% QoQ and 8.9% YoY; management cited a couple of Europe wins that should ramp.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 IT services revenue guided to $2.574B to $2.627B, or -1.5% to +0.5% sequential in constant currency.
Q2 guidance includes full-quarter Mindsprint revenue; Q1 included about two months of Mindsprint, versus 45 days assumed in prior guidance.
Management aims to return margin to the 17% to 17.5% band but would not give a timeline, citing volatility and continued AI investment.
Management said the client insourcing impact on BFSI is behind the company.
Management would not forecast beyond Q2 and said slipped BFSI deals are expected to close in Q2.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose QoQ only because of Mindsprint joiners; excluding them, headcount fell by 2,500.
Acquisition of Mindsprint closed in the quarter and is moving into execution.
AI-native business and platforms unit launched last quarter is building industry platforms, with the Wipro Ventures fund of $0.5B targeting AI, data and security startups.
Launched 10 Wipro Innovation Networks for clients and an Applied AI Center of Excellence for Anthropic Claude models.
Margin levers cited: automation and AI in fixed-price work, pyramid restructuring, G&A, and bench utilisation.
demand_pricing: Management described client spend as measured with longer decision cycles, with discretionary spend slower, while AI, data, cloud and cybersecurity remain funded.
Clients are reinvesting cost-optimisation and vendor-consolidation savings into AI, which management expects to revive discretionary transformation spend.
Large-deal pricing is competitive; traditional BPO and support budgets are compressing as AI takes share, and management says token costs push clients to total-cost-of-ownership pricing.
Management said AI-led Reimagine AI work (advisory, data priming, agent management) carries premium rate realisation and better margins than traditional deals.
Consumer is weak in APMEA; tech and communication strong in Americas; EMR modest in APMEA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was headcount added despite a guided sequential revenue decline, and is attrition under control?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount increase was from Mindsprint joiners; excluding them, headcount fell by 2,500 QoQ. Utilisation dipped slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BFSI decline client-specific, and will it hold back Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited slower ramp-ups on large deals and slower discretionary decisions. Europe and APMEA BFSI grew YoY, and Americas BFSI shows momentum from recent large wins.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins recover to the 17% to 17.5% band, and when do headwinds recede?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin drop reflected MSI impact, AI and deal investments, and acquisition integration. Management gave no timeline but cited cost, automation, pyramid and G&A levers; it will guide only one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Healthcare outlook and recovery timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Healthcare fell 2.6% QoQ and 3.0% YoY on US payer and provider budget pressure. Management sees AI-led claims and contact-centre opportunities but gave no recovery timeline beyond Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Did large deal bookings fall YoY due to timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Some decisions slipped into Q2. Management is pushing to close deals in month one or two rather than month three.

qa_highlights.question: How do margins look on AI-driven large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Large deals stay competitive with forward productivity baked in. Newer AI spend, data and advisory work is expected to be margin-accretive and carry premium realisation.

risks_watch: Americas remains soft, with Americas 2 down 7.3% YoY; recovery depends on BFSI large-deal ramp-ups.
Margin at 16% sits below the 17% to 17.5% target band; timing of recovery is unspecified and AI investment continues.
Large-deal bookings fell sharply YoY and some decisions slipped into Q2, so Q2 bookings and conversions are a watch item.
AI deflation of legacy and traditional BPO work could erode existing book; management says new AI services offset this.
Healthcare (US payers and providers) and EMR continue to decline; Q2 guidance assumes no recovery there.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI strategy and pipeline health but cautious on near-term demand. Management was evasive on margin timing and on growth beyond Q2, and it acknowledged slipped deals and margin pressure from large deals.
key_quotes: The AI disruption is expanding the market, not shrinking it.
In quarter 2, we are guiding for a sequential growth of -1.5% to +0.5% in constant currency terms.
Our mission is clearly to go back to the narrow band that we've been talking about, 17% to 17.5%.
Some of the decisions on some of these deals have actually slipped to quarter two.

adds.what: Mindsprint acquisition (closed this quarter, moving into execution); adds revenue from full quarter in Q2, not a company-built capacity addition

growth.why: Q2 FY27 guided to -1.5% to +0.5% sequential cc growth ($2.574B-$2.627B), with Mindsprint full-quarter contribution and $3.4B bookings ($1.6B large deals) as support; management gave no view beyond Q2 and no margin timeline for the 17-17.5% band, and utilisation dipped QoQ.
